stages.title: BIG BANG: HOT DENSE BEGINNING, EXPANSION AND EVIDENCE
stages.terms: The exam-safe formulation is an extremely hot, dense early state followed by expansion and cooling.
stages.mechanism: The exam-safe formulation is an extremely hot, dense early state followed by expansion and cooling.
stages.consequence: “Explosion” is misleading if it suggests matter flying from a centre into empty space.
stages.trap: Do not equate Big Bang with a bomb exploding at one point in pre-existing empty space.
stages.answer: The Big Bang denotes the expansion and cooling of an extremely hot, dense early universe about 13.8 billion years ago, not an explosion from one point into pre-existing empty space.

stages.title: GALAXIES AND THE MASS-CONTROLLED LIFE CYCLE OF STARS
stages.terms: Initial stellar mass controls core pressure and fusion rate, so it largely determines a star's lifetime, evolutionary path and final remnant.
stages.mechanism: Greater initial mass raises core temperature and fusion rate, causing massive stars to exhaust their nuclear fuel faster.
stages.consequence: Low-mass stars usually survive longer, whereas sufficiently massive stars evolve rapidly toward supernovae and compact remnants.
stages.trap: Do not infer that a larger fuel reserve makes a massive star longer-lived, because its fuel-consumption rate rises much more sharply.
stages.answer: Galaxies organise matter on the largest stellar scale, while initial mass is the controlling variable in the life cycle of an individual star.

stages.title: FORMATION AND CLASSIFICATION OF THE SOLAR SYSTEM
stages.terms: Technically, Formation And Classification Of The Solar System is analysed by relating Formation to Classification Of The Solar System, then testing the relationship through Terrestrial planets and Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.
stages.mechanism: The leading exam-safe model is gravitational collapse of a rotating gas-dust cloud about 4.6 billion years ago.

stages.answer: The Solar System formed through gravitational collapse and flattening of a rotating gas-dust nebula, followed by accretion that differentiated rocky inner planets from giant outer planets.

stages.title: EARTH'S SHAPE: OBLATE SPHEROID AND GEOID
stages.terms: Rotation produces a small equatorial bulge and polar flattening, so an oblate spheroid is the geometric approximation.
stages.mechanism: Rotation produces a small equatorial bulge and polar flattening, so an oblate spheroid is the geometric approximation.
stages.consequence: The geoid is the equipotential surface of Earth's gravity field that best approximates global mean sea level and conceptually continues beneath continents.
stages.trap: Earth is not a perfect sphere.
stages.answer: Earth is approximated geometrically as an oblate spheroid, while the geoid is the gravity-defined equipotential surface that best approximates global mean sea level.

stages.terms: Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the Equator, whereas longitude measures angular distance east or west of the Prime Meridian and provides the basis for time.
stages.mechanism: Longitude lines converge poleward; therefore one degree of longitude becomes shorter away from the Equator, while one degree of latitude remains nearly constant.

stages.title: LOCAL TIME, STANDARD TIME, UTC/GMT AND INTERNATIONAL DATE LINE
stages.terms: Anadyr lies west of the line and Nome east of it: Anadyr is a calendar day ahead, not behind.

stages.answer: Earth's rotation gives 15° of longitude per hour and 1° per four minutes; east is ahead, and crossing the International Date Line westward adds a calendar day while eastward subtracts one.

stages.title: MAGNETOSPHERE, SOLAR WIND, AURORA AND SPACE WEATHER
stages.terms: Technically, Magnetosphere, Solar Wind, Aurora And Space Weather is analysed by relating Magnetosphere to Solar Wind, then testing the relationship through Aurora and Space Weather.
stages.mechanism: India's low magnetic latitude reduces routine auroral visibility and high-latitude grid-current exposure, but equatorial ionospheric disturbance can still affect navigation and communication.

stages.answer: Aurora is the visible result of solar particles guided by the magnetosphere into the polar upper atmosphere, where collisions excite oxygen and nitrogen to emit light.

stages.title: EARTH'S INTERIOR THROUGH COMPOSITIONAL LAYERS AND SEISMIC EVIDENCE
stages.terms: India's location must be read through four linked ideas—absolute position, physical site, relational situation and territorial extent—because coordinates alone do not explain significance.

stages.answer: The disappearance of S-waves through the outer core and the refraction of P-waves create shadow zones that reveal a liquid outer core surrounding a solid inner core.

stages.title: ABSOLUTE COORDINATES, DIMENSIONS, AREA, RANK AND SHARE
stages.terms: Technically, Absolute Coordinates, Dimensions, Area, Rank And Share is analysed by relating Absolute Coordinates to Dimensions, then testing the relationship through Area and Rank.
stages.mechanism: The standard mainland envelope is 8°4'N–37°6'N and 68°7'E–97°25'E.

stages.title: TROPIC OF CANCER: EIGHT-STATE ORDER AND SIGNIFICANCE
stages.terms: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight states from Gujarat to Mizoram, but it is a solar reference parallel rather than an equal divider or climatic wall.
stages.mechanism: The Tropic of Cancer at 23°30'N is the northern overhead-Sun limit.

stages.title: EAST–WEST SOLAR-TIME SPREAD AND UNEQUAL DIMENSIONS
stages.terms: Technically, East–West Solar-Time Spread And Unequal Dimensions is analysed by relating East to West Solar-Time Spread, then testing the relationship through Unequal Dimensions and Eastern India.
stages.mechanism: Similar angular spans do not give equal kilometres because longitude degrees contract with latitude.
stages.consequence: Eastern India experiences local sunrise and noon earlier than western India, although clocks use one IST.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: the two-hour figure is an envelope calculation.
stages.answer: India's 29°18' longitudinal span produces about 117 minutes of local solar-time difference, even though one civil time is used across the country.

stages.title: HIMALAYA AND OCEAN AS FILTERS AND CONNECTORS
stages.terms: Filter explains both obstruction and selective passage; connector explains routes without denying risk.
stages.mechanism: Filter explains both obstruction and selective passage; connector explains routes without denying risk.
stages.consequence: The Himalaya obstructs extremely cold continental air, forces uplift of moisture-bearing winds and raises the cost of movement.

stages.answer: The Himalaya and surrounding seas act as selective filters and connectors: they raise movement costs and shape climate while still channeling exchange through passes, valleys and maritime routes.
